wiki_text: In December 2025, Sempra Infrastructure and Mexico's Comisión Federal de Electricidad (CFE) agreed to rescind their development agreement for the Vista Pacífico LNG export project at Topolobampo, Sinaloa, ending a roughly four-year development effort. Sempra disclosed the cancellation in its annual report (Form 10-K) filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on February 26, 2026, stating that "due to a change in the priorities of SI Partners and CFE, in December 2025 we agreed to rescind the existing development agreement." Shortly before the filing, Mexico's Comisión Nacional de Energía (CNE) denied Sempra Infrastructure a permit to construct the liquefaction plant. The project, planned at roughly 3–3.5 mtpa, had drawn opposition from more than twenty environmental organizations, fishing communities, and academic institutions over impacts to the Gulf of California, including seabed dredging for a floating liquefaction unit.

topic: Owner financial distress and CNE pipeline-permit denial (2025–2026)
wiki_text: Owner New Fortress Energy (NFE) entered severe financial distress in late 2025 and early 2026. Facing roughly US$5.7 billion of debt, NFE pursued a UK 'scheme of arrangement' (announced around March 17, 2026) intended to convert a large portion of its debt to equity — reducing the burden to about US$527 million in exchange for handing majority ownership to former creditors — with Chapter 11 bankruptcy as the alternative if creditors rejected the plan. Separately, in December 2025 Mexico's Comisión Nacional de Energía (CNE) denied NFE subsidiary Mexico FLNG Onshore the permit required to transport natural gas by pipeline to the Altamira facility, citing technical inconsistencies in the application; the ministry indicated the company could reapply after correcting the deficiencies. Trade-press reporting indicated that construction of the second Altamira liquefaction unit (Train 2) was placed on hold in December 2025 amid the cash crunch, and that NFE's most recent disclosures no longer listed the partially completed unit among its operating assets, instead referencing it as collateral for non-recourse loans.

In September 2025, Gato Negro LNG (developed by Houston-based Big River Energy and Gato Negro LNG) formalized an expansion of its Manzanillo, Colima liquefaction project, tripling planned capacity from 3 mtpa to 9 mtpa to be built in three phases: Phase 1 of 3 mtpa (about 0.5 Bcf/d), Phase 2 bringing the total to 6 mtpa (1.0 Bcf/d), and Phase 3 reaching the full 9 mtpa (1.5 Bcf/d) design. Commercial operations were targeted for 2030. The company reported that most required permits in Mexico and the United States had been obtained and that land acquisition in Manzanillo was complete, with the expansion backed by binding letters of intent for offtake, gas supply, and pipeline access to Permian/Waha gas. Reporting in April 2026 indicated the project's final investment decision had slipped about one year, to late 2027. (Note: the developer's website moved from gatonegro-lng.com to gatonegrolng.com.)
